title.narrative: Brazil: Support to New Bolsa Familia Conditional Cash Transfer Program

description.narrative: Brazil: Support to New Bolsa Familia Conditional Cash Transfer Program for Brazil has the development objectives to protect the income of poor families with children from 0 to 6 years of age and to mitigate risks that might damage those children's human capital. The project consists of one Component, the First Childhood Benefit for families with children from 0 to 6 years of age, which finances monthly conditional cash transfers to eligible families under Bolsa Familia (BF) to reinforce early childhood health and education, with compliance monitored through health checkups and preschool enrollment and attendance. Eligibility is verified through the Single Social Assistance Registry (Cadastro Unico) managed by the Ministry of Development, Social Assistance, Family, and Hunger Alleviation (MDS), and payments are delivered through Caixa Economica Federal (CEF) using digital accounts to ensure timely and secure access. Monitoring of conditionalities is carried out via the Monitoring System for Conditionalities (SICON), which consolidates information provided by health and education authorities, and program oversight includes results monitoring and evaluation conducted by the Project Implementation Unit within MDS. Beneficiary engagement and grievance resolution are supported by established grievance redress mechanisms in line with national legislation, with performance tracked against service standards to ensure timely responses. The Component is implemented within Brazil's adaptive social protection system to strengthen resilience to shocks, with priority given to women as designated recipients and enhancements to data quality and interoperability to maintain accurate beneficiary records and continuous service delivery.
The objective of the project is to protect income and mitigate the risks of damaging human capital of poor families with children and youth.

comment.narrative: This indicator previously captured only children benefiting from the First Childhood Benefit (Beneficio Primeira Infância – BPI). It has now been adjusted under the updated/consolidated CRI methodology to include all household members in families receiving the benefit. Corrected figures for previous periods and target are: 24,720,228 (Dec-31-2024), 23,661,159 (Jun-30-2025) and 24,800,000 (Abr-30-2026).

comment.narrative: This indicator previously captured all household members receiving Bolsa Familia residing in municipalities vulnerable to climate castastrophies. It has now been adjusted under the updated/consolidated CRI methodology to include all household members in households receiving the First Childhood Benefit (Beneficio Primeira Infância – BPI) residing in municipalities vulnerable to climate catastrophies. The target has also been updated to 6,800,000 using the December 2024 value as a reference.
